summary: Add the package's strict declaration schema — the eleven fields a consumer declares — refusing an unknown or a missing required field at load, naming the field and the valid set.
tests: the declaration schema parses a declaration naming every field
an unknown declaration field is refused, naming the field and the valid set
a missing required declaration field is refused, naming the field
pins: the package exports map resolves ./harness to the built harness entry point
acceptance: harness/declaration.ts parses a full declaration and refuses both an unknown field and a missing required one, each refusal naming the field.
notes: runner types against harness/runner.ts. No field names an engine artifact path, a verdict field, or a prior-attempt mode. Shape alone; consumers are the cite resolver and the chain factory, later entries. 396b90e reverted on the hand-restated export list in harnessPackaging.test.ts — make it derive from the module (engineering.md, *A seam gate reads what the real writer wrote*). Leaves no chain-side twin.

new.description: the six fields, their caps and their hints
the render, the consumer add, the removal refusal

summary: Extract the package's entry extension — summary, per, acceptance, tests[], pins[], notes with their caps and hints — as a value a consumer adds to but cannot remove from.
tests: the package's entry extension declares summary, per, acceptance, tests, pins and notes
a consumer field is merged into the entry extension beside the package's own
a consumer extension that drops a package field is refused, naming the field
a summary past the package's cap is refused
acceptance: harness/entryExtension.ts renders the six fields into a prompt schema and refuses a consumer extension that removes one.
notes: Chain-side twin at .flume/chain.ts:117 until the cutover. Consumed by the judges, the gates and the factory. Renders through the engine's renderSchemaForPrompt — one declaration per field, never a second hint copy in a prompt.

new.description: record dirs, the per-tag note path, the byte cap, the pending predicate
the note path, and the live/empty window both asserted

summary: Extract the record conventions the inbox slice drains — the record dirs, the per-tag note path, the byte cap — into one package-owned home under a declared state root.
tests: the note path for an entry tag is that tag's file under the state root's notes dir
a record directory holding a file reports the record window live
a record directory holding no file reports the record window empty
acceptance: harness/records.ts names the record dirs, the per-tag note path and the byte cap under a declared state root, and reports whether any record is pending.
notes: One home so the gate, the prompt and the liveness predicate cannot name different files. Twins at .flume/chain.ts:25 and :171. The byte cap is the package's value, not a declaration knob — the discipline it enforces is the package's.

new.description: the declared state fields, their schema, and the read/write accessor
the two cursors, the continuation signal, the refusal, the absent case

summary: Add the package's plan-state accessor: the derive and sweep cursors and the continuation signal as declared fields of a typed artifact, never a line regexed out of prose.
tests: the plan state accessor reads the derive and sweep cursors as fields
the plan state accessor reads the continuation signal and its covered set
a plan state artifact missing a required field is refused, naming the field
an absent plan state artifact reads as no cursor rather than throwing
acceptance: harness/planState.ts reads and writes both cursors and the continuation signal as typed fields and refuses a malformed artifact by name.
notes: Typed artifact, not a parser over prose — the section forecloses the regex, and pending.json is the precedent for agent-written, schema-gated plan output. The narrative state.md carries today moves to the plan commit body (collaboration.md, *Artifacts are the present; git is the log*). Migrating the live .flume/plan/state.md is chain-side and rides the cutover. Twin at .flume/chain.ts:563.

summary: Derive the consumer's state-root ignore lines from the engine's path record, and drive that output against this repo's .gitignore so a retired runtime name cannot linger.
tests: the consumer ignore set prefixes every engine runtime path with the declared state root
the consumer ignore set names no path outside the engine's path record
this repository's .gitignore carries no state-root line the derived set does not name
acceptance: harness/ignores.ts derives .flume's ignore lines from the engine's path record and a test drives that output against this repo's .gitignore.
notes: Imports src/paths.ts directly, as harness/vitestRunner.ts does, so src/index.ts widens for no one. Retires .gitignore's .flume/last-tick.json. Not RUNTIME_IGNORES (src/job.ts) — that is the job dir's set and stays; this is the consumer root's, derived rather than copied, so it is not a fourth copy of the list parked in open-questions.md.

summary: Add the package's per resolver: the path matches a specLocus glob and is in the gated commit, the section is a heading in it, and a consumer may declare a resolver that keys sections instead.
tests: a per cite whose path matches no specLocus glob is refused, naming the path
a per cite whose section is no heading at the gated commit is refused, naming the section
a declared resolver keys a section without changing the verdict shape
acceptance: harness/citeResolver.ts resolves a per against a declared specLocus at a commit and yields one verdict shape whether the section is found by heading or by a declared resolver.
notes: The at-ref reader is injected, not imported, so every case stays in the fast lane. .flume/chain.ts's perResolvesGate and sectionOf are the chain-side copy this retires at the cutover.

new.description: the tests[]/pins[] judge over the runner interface
the refusal, the green-on-base fact, the pins lane, the empty case

summary: Extract the tests[]/pins[] judge onto the runner interface — named lines green on the merged tree and red at the base, pins green only — reporting green-on-base as a fact.
tests: a tests[] line no passing test carries is refused, naming the line
a tests[] line already green at the base is reported as a named fact
a pins[] line is judged on the merged tree and never run at the base
a judge over no named lines reports the empty case rather than a green verdict
acceptance: harness/judge.ts judges an entry's tests[] and pins[] through a declared runner and hands back the per-line verdict, green-on-base included.
notes: Drives harness/runner.ts and never names vitest; the runner cuts over with the judge that drives it (the cutover ruling). Twins: .flume/vitestJudge.ts and .flume/chain.ts:812. The reported fact is what retires .flume/chain.ts:632's regex over the gate's own message (engineering.md, *A fact the engine holds is reported, never rediscovered*).

new.description: the per, records, clean-tree and pending gates as one set per phase
one refusal per gate, plus the ordering

summary: Extract the four gates the discipline needs — per, records, clean-tree, and the pending gate wired to the consumer's fence — as the package's always-first gate set per phase.
tests: the per gate refuses a commit whose cited file is not in it, naming the tag
the records gate refuses a record written outside the tick's own tag
the records gate refuses a record past the byte cap
the clean-tree gate refuses a leftover path the phase may not write
the package's gates precede a consumer's declared gates for the same phase
acceptance: harness/gates.ts returns the four gates for a phase ahead of a consumer's declared ones, each refusing on its own case.
notes: The per gate wraps HARNESS-CITE-RESOLVER's verdict rather than re-resolving it; the pending gate takes the declaration's fence as targetFence and the package's entry extension. Twins at .flume/chain.ts:264, :340, :386.

new.description: the default next-phase ladder and the refusal leg
each rung, the refusal route, the no-self-rewake case, the override

summary: Extract the package's default handoff — first live slice, else build while the engine reports anything pickable, else hibernate — with a build refusal routing to the inbox slice.
tests: the default handoff names the first live slice ahead of build
the default handoff names build when no slice is live and the engine reports a pickable entry
the default handoff hibernates when no slice is live and nothing is pickable
a build tick the chain declined routes to the inbox slice whatever is pickable
a slice that committed nothing is not named by its own handoff
a declared handoff replaces the package's default
acceptance: harness/handoff.ts maps the engine's reported pickable set and no-commit facts onto the next phase, and a consumer's declaration replaces it.
notes: Liveness comes from harness/records.ts and harness/planState.ts; the slice set is a parameter until the factory exists. Reads the engine's reported pickableAfter and no-commit facts only — never a re-parse of an agent stream. Twins at .flume/chain.ts:686 and :920.

edit.description: the second bin entry, and the files allowlist covering the template

summary: Ship flume-harness, the bin the package carries beside the engine's flume, and its init verb: the declaration skeleton, the state root, the ignore set and PROTOCOL.md.
tests: flume-harness init writes a declaration skeleton the package's schema parses
flume-harness init writes the state root and its derived ignore lines
flume-harness init writes PROTOCOL.md from the package's own template
flume-harness init refuses a state root that already exists rather than overwriting it
pins: the engine's flume bin exposes no harness verb
acceptance: node bin/flume-harness.js init in an empty repo writes a declaration the package's schema parses, the state root, the ignore set and PROTOCOL.md.
notes: The shim is bin/flume.js's shape — argv through, stdio inherited, exit code out, no options of its own (spec/cli.md, *Distribution*). The files allowlist must cover the template: tsc emits no .md into dist/, and CI asserts the packed set both ways. The dependency add shells the consumer's package manager. The engine's verb set stays closed — that is why the verb lives here.
